Tropical Depression 2C—expected to organize into Tropical Storm Moke—is running into atmospheric speed bumps that will keep it from building into a major hurricane. Moderate upper-level wind shear and pockets of dry air are tilting the system and disrupting its convective core. While the system won’t pack a damaging wind punch, its broad footprint means it will act like a giant, moisture-rich sponge moving across the region.
